text:
marta: Heads-up — saw a customer report where routing picked Dedicated pool but quota was charged to a downstream service account and the request later got throttled. Repro steps attached.
sam: Oof. Do we have a deterministic precedence between X-Custom-Auth (tenant) vs Authorization bearer (service) vs User-Agent-derived tenant? I thought auth header > signed route.
raj: We do, but there are a couple of edge cases: when Authorization maps to a service identity with no tenant, UA inference can win, and the routing decision uses UA -> dedicated because of client-affinity rules.
marta: Exact. In their replay: curl with `-H "Authorization: Bearer svc-abc" -H "X-Tenant: tenant-123" -H "User-Agent: RedwoodClient/2.1.0"`
marta: Our gateway matched on UA affinity and routed to dedicated-pool-1. Quota enforcement later resolved to svc-abc (service account) which had a tighter reserved quota, so requests started failing under load.
sam: That explains the mismatch. Two problems: (1) decision surface uses UA which is spoofable and (2) telemetry doesn't attach routing provenance to logs so billing/owner attribution is fuzzy.
raj: Proposal: 1) add a routing provenance header `X-Redwood-Routing: "src=ua;rule=affinity;decider=edgesvc"` on responses and internal logs. 2) change precedence so explicit tenant headers (X-Tenant, X-Customer-ID) win over UA-inferred routing, unless there's a signed routing token.
consoleux: UX: expose a compact rollout view in Console that shows weight of signals (auth, tenant header, UA, signed-route) and the active precedence table for a route. That will make canaries less mysterious.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary started for routing-provenance v1 -> 5% traffic to edgesvc-canary (2024-11-08 15:12 UTC)
sam: +1 on provenance header. Also we should ensure this header is only emitted internally (or for customer debug if enabled) to avoid leaking routing policy details to end clients.
marta: For testing, I pushed a test harness to reproduce: `scripts/repro/routing_mismatch.sh` which sends permutations and prints body, response headers. Example curl used in repro:

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer svc-abc" -H "X-Tenant: tenant-123" -H "User-Agent: RedwoodClient/2.1.0" \
  https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate
```

marta: Suggested rollout: 5% canary with provenance header enabled in internal logs + metrics. After 24h if no mismatches, flip precedence change behind a feature flag, canary 5% -> 20% -> 100%.
raj: I'll draft the precedence change RFC and add unit tests for the router: permutations of (auth, x-tenant, ua, signed-token) and expected route. Also add e2e that asserts `X-Redwood-Routing` matches decision and that quota attribution maps to the chosen principal.
sam: Also add a telemetry tag `routing.decision_hash` to traces so we can correlate requests that later get throttled to the original routing decision.
consoleux: I'll wire the Console canary panel to show those traces and a small histogram of mismatches (route vs quota owner) so PMs can watch.
marta: OK owners: raj (impl router precedence + tests), sam (quota attribution audit + telemetry), consoleux (console UI), infra-bot will manage canary. I'll open a short ticket and link here.
marta: thanks all. :thumbsup:"
